stage1.impression: A night canal quay with a rim-lit, multicoloured ring globe on a black plinth, a hard white spot throwing a tinted shadow across the paving, and a row of gabled facades with lit windows across the water. The globe reads instantly and the coloured shadow is a real idea, but the frame reads as a competent CG render rather than a photograph: the facades are one repeated module with flat, evenly lit window cards and no brick; the paving is a uniform tiled texture; the spot pool is a cold, theatrical ellipse with a near-black hole beside it; and the street lamp floods the left foreground brighter than the work itself. A jury would see a specific work, but in a generic render of a place, not Amsterdam at night.

blocking_9: The far facades must read as real Amsterdam canal houses: varied gables, widths and heights, visible brick, and windows lit unevenly from inside (lamps, curtains, falloff) rather than flat, uniformly lit panes
The coloured shadow must be the brightest, most saturated thing on the ground: all six tints legible in it, with the left foreground paving darker than the spot pool
The spot must read as warm-neutral festival light that matches the room's 2700 to 3000 K world, not a cold 5000 K stage ellipse with a blue-white cast
The paving and kerb must read as worn Amsterdam brick klinkers and granite at 1:1, with variation, wet patches or grime, not a uniform tiled texture
The plinth and the base of the globe must hold detail instead of merging into the shadow (plinth median about 12)
No visible grain in the lit paving; no props hidden half behind the work (the bicycle)

defects.what: Facades are one repeated module of identical windows; lit panes are flat cream or white cards (median about 160) with no interiors, no brick texture, no gables or roofline in frame
The street lamp floods the left foreground paving to median 121, far brighter than the shadow area (73) and the globe region (34): the eye goes to empty paving, not the work
The spot pool is a hard, cold, blue-white ellipse (5000 K against a 3500 K balance); its rim at about 156 outshines the shadow, which reads mostly pink-mauve with the six tints barely separable
The plinth is crushed nearly black (median 12 to 18) and merges with its own shadow; no edge sheen or blackened-steel texture
Paving is a uniform, regular brick texture with no wear, staining, joints filled with grime or variation: reads as a CG tile
Visible noise and grain in the lit paving inside the spot pool at 1:1
A bicycle is half hidden behind the globe's rings, reading as clutter tangled with the work
The figures across the water are tiny, stiff, isolated silhouettes; read as placed props
The barrier ring's rope reads as a thin black wire, slicing through the shadow and the foreground
Water reflections are plausible but uniform; the far quay wall and waterline are featureless dark bands

changes.problem: The street lamp at left lights empty foreground paving brighter than the work and its shadow, pulling the eye away from the subject.

evidence.measured: lum_median 120.9 vs. shadow area [520,470,720,620] median 72.8 and globe region median 33.6

change.setting: the street lamps: 2 x point, power
change.to: 45 W (and move the nearer one so its pool falls behind the camera-left bollard rather than across the foreground)

changes.expected: Left foreground drops to a dim warm glow around median 45 to 60; the spot pool and coloured shadow become the brightest ground in the frame.

changes.problem: The spot is a cold blue-white stage ellipse that reads as theatre lighting and desaturates the coloured shadow.

evidence.measured: pool rim band peaks at about 156 with r 52 / g 42 / b 41 in the region and a visibly blue-white cast against the 3500 K balance; shadow [520,470,720,620] r 90 g 66 b 67, tints merge into pink-mauve

changes.expected: The pool reads warm-neutral, of a piece with the city's 2700 K light, and the six tints in the shadow separate; the pool's neutral rim stays near neutral (r and b within 15 of each other).

changes.problem: The coloured shadow, the point of this frame, is too dim and too pale relative to the pool around it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 72.8, lum_p95 138.5; pool rim about 156 (profile [450,620,470,700]); tints barely distinguishable in the crop

change.setting: the hard spot: power and cone
change.to: 1400 W, cone 13 deg (aimed at [0.6, -2.2, 0.0] so the pool hugs the shadow and wastes less light on bare paving), with a soft edge blend of about 0.25

changes.expected: The shadow's coloured area rises to median about 95 to 120 with distinct tints, and the pool's edge softens into a natural falloff rather than a cut ellipse.

changes.problem: The far facades are one repeated module with flat, evenly lit window panes and no brick, which reads as CG and not as an Amsterdam canal.

evidence.measured: lit panes median about 160 to 164, flat with lum_p5 26 to 34 only at mullions; identical window grid across all bays; no brick texture visible at 1:1

change.setting: the houses across: materials and windows
change.from: 0.32 of windows lit, glow 0.1, one repeated facade, smooth brick
change.to: 0.2 of windows lit with glow varied 0.03 to 0.12 per window, warm interior falloff (a lamp, curtains or a ceiling behind each lit pane), brick with a visible bond and mortar normal/roughness, and varied bay widths and heights (if the facade asset allows); tilt the camera so a few gables show

changes.expected: Lit windows read as rooms, not cards, mostly in the 90 to 150 range with variation; the facade band reads as brick.

changes.problem: The plinth is crushed nearly black and merges with the shadow under the globe, so the work has no base.

change.setting: the far quay's fill / rims' glow
change.from: fill 0.4 W/m2 at 2400 K; rims' glow 0.18
change.to: fill 0.8 W/m2 at 2400 K, plus a low uplight or the rims' glow at 0.22 so the plinth's top edge and the blackened steel pick up a soft coloured sheen

changes.expected: Plinth face reads as dark blackened steel with a visible top edge and uneven sheen, median about 20 to 30.

changes.problem: The paving reads as a uniform brick tile texture, a strong CG cue at this camera height.

evidence.measured: lum_range 15.5 (p5 38.5, p95 53.9): almost no variation across a large stretch of paving

change.to: brick klinker with per-brick colour and roughness variation, darker grimy joints, a few damp patches (low roughness) that catch the spot and the windows, and a granite kerb with chipped edge

changes.expected: Paving in the foreground shows texture and local variation; lum_range in a quiet patch rises to about 30 or more.

changes.problem: The bicycle is half hidden behind the globe, tangling its outline with the rings; the barrier rope reads as wire slicing through the shadow.

evidence.measured: bicycle frame visible through the rings in crop at 2x

change.from: a bicycle behind the globe; rope at 0.45 m as thin black line
change.to: move the bicycle to lean against the right-hand bollard near [3.5, -1.0], clear of the globe; thicken the rope to a 30 mm dull hemp or dark-red rope with slight sag between posts

changes.expected: The globe's silhouette reads clean against the water; a sign of life sits at the right edge; the barrier reads as a soft rope, not a wire.

changes.problem: Visible grain in the lit paving of the spot pool at 1:1.

evidence.measured: grain visible in the 2x crop of the pool and shadow

changes.expected: Clean pool with paving joints intact, no blotch or speckle.

out_of_scope.request: Make the disc faces carry more visible tint so the shadow's colours separate more
out_of_scope.why: The discs' colours and clear, rim-lit faces are fixed by the card; tint strength of the faces is part of the globe's design.

out_of_scope.request: Brief mismatch: the critic prompt describes judging a listening-bar interior with one EARF speaker, but this image and card are an outdoor light-festival entry
out_of_scope.why: Judged against the card's own aim (a jury night photograph of the work in place) and the prompt's photographic bar; the 'room', 'cozy' and 'acrylic speaker' criteria were read as applying to the work and its site.
